newsitem.title: UK: Air Foyle ships Ericsson telecoms to Chile.
newsitem.headline: Air Foyle ships Ericsson telecoms to Chile.

text.p: UK-based cargo charter airline Air Foyle said an Antonov AN-124 aircraft left Luxembourg today carrying 115 tonnes of telecommunications equipment to the Chilean capital, Santiago.
The equipment manufactured by the Swedish telecoms group, Ericsson had previously been shipped from Stockholm to Luxembourg, an Air Foyle spokeswoman told Reuters.
Ericsson has won contracts this year from Startel, Chile's largest wireless network operator, for expansion of the latter's network.

Air Foyle, which also acts as general sales agent for the Antonov Design Bureau (ADB), also said that in late May it and ADB carried an urgently need 60 tonne diesel engine from Piura on the Peruvian coast to Iquitos in eastern Peru.

The flight was undertaken on behalf of Electro-Peru, the country's electricity utility, who needed the engine to restore full power at Iquitos where the power station was operating at only two-thirds capacity, Air Foyle said in a statement.
It added that a specially modified ramp and trailer unit had to be devised to assist in handling, and especially offloading as there were no cranes or hydraulic vehicles available to help in Iquitos.
